mainTopic: Why wages for work with יין נסך are a rabbinic קנס, and what the parallel קנס on donkey drivers carrying שביעית produce means.
overview: The משנה rules that a Jew hired to work with יין נסך may not benefit from his wage. If he was hired for other work, his wage is permitted, even if he moved a barrel of יין נסך along the way. The same rule applies to renting out a donkey. The גמרא asks why the wage is forbidden, and two suggested reasons are knocked down: one from ערלה and כלאי הכרם, and one from שביעית. רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן explains that it is a קנס the חכמים made, and that a similar קנס applies to donkey drivers who carry שביעית produce, whose wage 'is שביעית'. The גמרא asks what that means. Paying them with שביעית produce seems like forbidden trading, and the idea that their money becomes holy is disproved by a ברייתא. אביי answers that they really are paid with שביעית produce, but it is handed over in a permitted way. He begins bringing a proof from a משנה in מעשר שני, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Hiring a worker for libation wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that wages for working with יין נסך are forbidden, but wages for other work are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: If someone hires a worker to work with him on יין נסך, the worker's wage is forbidden. If he hired him for some other job, the wage is permitted, even if he told him: 'Move this barrel of יין נסך for me from one place to another.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets out its first rule: what matters is what the worker was hired to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the job itself is working with יין נסך, the money earned is forbidden. If the job is something else, the pay is for that other work. A small side task with יין נסך does not ruin the whole wage.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured or used for idol worship; forbidden in benefit

steps.confusionAlert: Carrying a barrel of יין נסך is not what makes the wage forbidden. The question is what job he was hired for in the first place.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who hires a worker
phrases.notes: The one hiring here is a non-Jew, and the worker is a Jew.

phrases.english: to work with him on libation wine
his wage is forbidden
if he hired him to do other work with him
even though he said to him
"Move for me a barrel of libation wine
from place to place"
his wage is permitted

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wage for work with יין נסך is forbidden. A wage for other work is permitted, even if the worker incidentally moved יין נסך.

steps.title: Renting a donkey to carry libation wine
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to renting out a donkey: rent paid for carrying יין נסך is forbidden, but rent paid for riding is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone rents a donkey to carry יין נסך on it, the rental fee is forbidden. If he rented it to ride on, the fee is permitted, even if the non-Jew put his jug of wine on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the same idea to an animal that is rented out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, the purpose of the rental decides the law. Renting the donkey in order to carry יין נסך makes the fee forbidden. A jug placed on the donkey along the way does not change a rental that was made for riding.

phrases.english: One who rents the donkey
to carry libation wine on it
its rental fee is forbidden
if he rented it to sit on it

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִנִּיחַ גּוֹי לְגִינוֹ עָלֶיהָ
phrases.english: even though the non-Jew placed his jug on it
its rental fee is permitted

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשּׂוֹכֵר אֶת הַחֲמוֹר לְהָבִיא עָלֶיהָ יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel case using a donkey instead of a worker
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rent paid for carrying יין נסך is forbidden. Rent paid for riding is permitted, even if wine was placed on the donkey.

steps.title: Why is the wage forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the משנה and offers a first suggestion: since יין נסך is forbidden in benefit, its wage is forbidden too.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is the reason the wage is forbidden? Should we say that since יין נסך is forbidden in benefit, the wage is also forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the wage is forbidden and tests a first possible answer. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested reason is simple: if the item is forbidden, the money that comes from it must be forbidden too. The word אילימא tells you this idea is about to be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
Forbidden to get any benefit from

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason his wage is forbidden?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא, הוֹאִיל וְיֵין נֶסֶךְ אָסוּר בַּהֲנָאָה
phrases.english: If we say: since libation wine is forbidden in benefit
his wage is also forbidden

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the wage for work with יין נסך is forbidden

steps.title: Challenge from ערלה and כלאי הכרם
steps.stepSummary: ערלה and כלאי הכרם are forbidden in benefit, yet money from selling them can be used for קידושין. So money from a forbidden item is not automatically forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But ערלה and כלאי הכרם are forbidden in benefit, and we learned in a משנה: if someone sold them and used the money to marry a woman, she is married!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the first suggestion by pointing to items that are also forbidden in benefit, yet the money received for them is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If money from a forbidden item were forbidden, the קידושין could not work, because a man cannot marry with forbidden money. Since the קידושין does work, the money must be permitted. So 'forbidden in benefit' cannot be the reason the wage is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years; forbidden in benefit
Mixed plantings in a vineyard; forbidden in benefit

phrases.english: But there are orlah and mixed vineyard plantings
which are forbidden in benefit
and we learned: if he sold them and betrothed a woman with their money
she is betrothed!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עׇרְלָה וְכִלְאֵי הַכֶּרֶם דַּאֲסוּרִין בַּהֲנָאָה
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that being forbidden in benefit makes the wage forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other items that are forbidden in benefit do not make their money forbidden, as shown by valid קידושין with that money.

steps.title: Second suggestion: it passes its status to its money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests instead that יין נסך is like עבודה זרה, which passes its forbidden status onto the money it is exchanged for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the reason is that it passes its status onto its money, like עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first reason fails, the גמרא offers a stronger reason for why the wage is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עבודה זרה is different from ערלה, because its forbidden status moves onto money received in exchange for it. If יין נסך has the same rule, then the wage counts as the price of the wine and is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Its status passes onto its money

phrases.english: Rather, since it transfers its status to its money
like idol worship

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הוֹאִיל וְתוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו כַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything forbidden in benefit makes its wage forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: יין נסך, like עבודה זרה, passes its status to its money

steps.title: Challenge from שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: שביעית produce also passes its status to its money, yet a worker's wage for picking it is permitted unless the money was given for the produce itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But שביעית produce passes its status onto its money, and we learned in a משנה: if one says to a worker, 'Here is this דינר, pick vegetables for me with it today,' the wage is forbidden. If he says, 'Pick vegetables for me today,' the wage is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second suggestion with a case where something passes its status to money, yet a plain wage for work stays permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the דינר is tied to the vegetables, it is like buying שביעית produce, so the money becomes holy. When the pay is simply for a day of work, the money is permitted. By the same logic, a wage for working with יין נסך should be permitted, since it is pay for labor and not the price of the wine.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh (שמיטה) year and its holy produce

phrases.english: But there is Sabbatical produce, which transfers its status to its money
and we learned: one who says to a worker
"Here is this dinar
gather vegetables for me with it today"
his wage is forbidden
"Gather vegetables for me today"
his wage is permitted!

steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that passing status to money explains the forbidden wage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שביעית also passes status to money, yet a plain wage for labor is permitted. So the יין נסך wage should be permitted too.

steps.title: It is a קנס from the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן explains that the forbidden wage is a קנס the חכמים imposed, both for יין נסך and for donkey drivers.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is a penalty the חכמים imposed on donkey drivers and on יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer: the wage is not forbidden by strict logic but by a special rabbinic penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both earlier reasons failed because by pure law a wage for labor should be permitted. רבי יוחנן admits this and explains that the חכמים added a penalty here. He also mentions a second penalty, for donkey drivers, which the גמרא will explain next.
steps.whatToRemember: The wage for working with יין נסך is forbidden only because of a קנס from the חכמים, not because money from forbidden items is automatically forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because the rule is a קנס, it stays limited to the cases the חכמים penalized. That explains why other work, or a side task, leaves the wage permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Yochanan said
It is a penalty that the Sages imposed
on donkey drivers and with libation wine

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question after both suggested reasons were rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wage is forbidden because of the wine's own status
steps.terutzMaskana: The wage is forbidden as a קנס of the חכמים

steps.title: What is the donkey drivers' penalty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the יין נסך penalty was already explained and asks what the donkey drivers' penalty is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The יין נסך penalty is what we said. What is the donkey drivers' penalty?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of the second penalty רבי יוחנן mentioned. This sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The יין נסך penalty is the משנה's own case. The donkey drivers' penalty is new, so the גמרא needs a source for it.

phrases.english: Libation wine: that which we said
Donkey drivers: what is it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the penalty on donkey drivers refers to

steps.title: Donkey drivers' wage is שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that donkey drivers who worked with שביעית produce have a wage that 'is שביעית'. The גמרא will next ask what this means.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: donkey drivers who worked with שביעית produce, their wage has the status of שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא that shows the donkey drivers' penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By strict law their pay is just for labor, as we saw with the worker in step 6. The ברייתא says their wage 'is שביעית' as a penalty, but it does not yet say what that means. The next steps test two readings, and אביי in step 14 settles on one.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two parallel קנסות: wages for work with יין נסך are forbidden, and donkey drivers who carry שביעית produce have a wage that 'is שביעית'. Steps 10–14 explain what that means.

phrases.english: As it is taught: donkey drivers who were working
with Sabbatical produce
their wage is Sabbatical produce

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: הַחַמָּרִין שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹשִׂין מְלָאכָה בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: As a penalty, the ברייתא rules that donkey drivers who work with שביעית produce have a wage that 'is שביעית'. Its exact meaning is clarified in steps 10-14.

steps.title: What does 'their wage is שביעית' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא meant when it said the donkey drivers' wage is שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does it mean that 'their wage is שביעית'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's words mean. This question sets up two possible readings that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'their wage is שביעית' can be read in more than one way. The גמרא is about to test each reading to see which one works.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year (שמיטה) and its produce, which has special holiness

phrases.english: What does "their wage is שביעית" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 9 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to understand the phrase 'their wage is שביעית'.

steps.title: Paying with שביעית produce would be trading with it
steps.stepSummary: If the drivers are paid with שביעית produce, the employer is paying a debt with it, and the Torah says שביעית produce is for eating, not for business.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we give them their wage from שביעית produce, then this employer is paying his debt with שביעית produce. But the Torah said 'for eating', and not for trading!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first reading: the drivers are paid with שביעית produce. It rejects this reading right away because it seems to break a Torah rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wage is a debt the employer owes. Paying a debt with שביעית produce counts as using it for business. The פסוק says the produce is 'for eating', which teaches it is not for trading.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a possible reading in order to test it)

phrases.english: If you say that we give them
a wage from שביעית produce,
it turns out this one is paying his debt
with שביעית produce,
but the Torah said: "for eating"
and not for trading!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּיָהֲבִינַן לְהוּ שָׂכָר מִפֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers the first reading of the question in step 10 and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the drivers are paid with שביעית produce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Paying a wage with שביעית produce is paying a debt with it, which is trading. The פסוק 'לאכלה' rules out trading.

steps.title: Second reading: the wage money becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the phrase means that the money the drivers receive takes on the holiness of שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that their wage becomes holy with the holiness of שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reading failed, the גמרא offers a second one. Their payment is ordinary money, but that money itself takes on שביעית holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading the employer does not hand over שביעית produce, so there is no problem of trading. Instead, the wage money gets שביעית rules, the same way money exchanged for שביעית produce does.

keyTerms.meaning: The holiness of שביעית, which brings special rules for how the item may be used

phrases.english: Rather, it means that their wage is holy
with the holiness of שביעית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the reading that was rejected in step 11 with a different one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the ברייתא's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The drivers are paid with שביעית produce itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drivers are paid with ordinary money, and that money takes on שביעית holiness.

steps.title: A worker's plain wage does not become holy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a worker is hired with a דינר to gather vegetables, his wage is permitted unless the דינר is paid as the value of the vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does the wage really become holy? It was taught: If someone says to a worker, 'Here is this דינר, and gather vegetables for me today,' his wage is permitted. If he says, 'Gather vegetables for me today for it,' his wage is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second reading. A ברייתא shows that a wage paid for work does not take on שביעית holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, money paid for the worker's labor stays ordinary. Only money paid as the price of the vegetables becomes forbidden. The donkey drivers are paid for their labor, like the first case, so their wage should not become holy.

keyTerms.meaning: But does it really...? (a question that doubts the claim)

steps.confusionAlert: The two cases in the ברייתא differ by one small word, 'בּוֹ' (for it). Without it, the dinar pays for the work and is permitted. With it, the dinar is the price of the vegetables and is forbidden.

phrases.english: But is it really holy?
But it was taught: One who says to a worker:
"Here is this dinar for you,
and gather vegetables for me today"
his wage is permitted,
"gather vegetables for me today for it"
phrases.notes: 'בּוֹ' (for it) means the דינר is paid as the price of the vegetables, not for the work.

phrases.english: his wage is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second reading proposed in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the drivers' wage money takes on שביעית holiness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא shows that money paid for labor stays permitted, and only money paid as the price of the produce becomes forbidden. The drivers are paid for labor.

steps.title: אביי: they are paid with produce, but in a permitted way
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the drivers really are paid with שביעית produce, and there is no trading problem because it is given to them in a permitted way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Really, we give him his wage from שביעית produce. And as for what bothers you, that it is 'for eating' and not for trading: he gives it to him in a permitted way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי goes back to the first reading, that the wage is paid with שביעית produce. He answers the 'not for trading' problem from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in step 11 was that paying a wage with שביעית produce counts as trading. אביי says the produce is handed over in a permitted way, not as a direct payment of the debt, so it is not trading.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (goes back to an earlier option and defends it)
And as for what is difficult for you

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the same act can be forbidden or allowed depending on how it is set up. Handing over שביעית produce as a direct payment is trading, but handing it over in a permitted way is not.

phrases.english: אביי said:
Really, we give him
a wage from שביעית produce,
and as for what bothers you,
"for eating" and not for trading,
it is that he gives it to him in a permitted way,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם יָהֲבִינַן לֵיהּ שָׂכָר מִפֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second reading fails in step 13, אביי returns to the first reading and answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defends the first reading by describing a permitted way of handing over the produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving a wage from שביעית produce is always trading with it.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the produce is handed over in a permitted way, it is not trading, so the drivers can be paid with it.

steps.title: אביי begins a proof from a משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts quoting a משנה that shows a permitted way to hand over holy produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A person should not say to his friend:
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins quoting a משנה to support his answer. The quote continues on the next amud, so this line is only the setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'כדתנן' signal that a משנה is coming to back up the idea of giving 'in a permitted way'. The content of the משנה has not appeared yet.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: As we learned: A person should not say to his friend:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מעשר שני 3:1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing a source to support אביי's answer in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that שביעית produce can be handed over in a permitted way.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in מעשר שני 3:1, which continues on the next amud.
